extracted.intended_audience: investigators applying for NIH/NIAID R21 grants (biomedical researchers preparing grant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: NIH peer review summary statement and criteria used to evaluate R21 grant applications, covering scientific review criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment), compliance items, scoring, and budget recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: An overall judgment of the likelihood that the project will have a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Reviewers' narrative overall impact summarizes major strengths and weaknesses (e.g., 'An excellent application...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress in the field that the project addresses and the degree to which the project will advance scientific knowledge or clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer comments indicate strengths such as: potential to reveal gene-specific post-transcriptional vs post-translational control; producing genome-wide data of enormous interest to the field; suitability of organism as model system. Weaknesses should be noted (e.g., uncertainty about the importance of differentiating specific subforms or difficulties separating cell types). Reviewers list specific strengths/weaknesses in bullets under Significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the experience, track record, and appropriateness of the project leadership and collaborators to carry out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer guidance includes evaluating productivity, relevant technical and leadership experience, history of collaboration, and ability to manage large datasets. Strengths cited include extensive experience, long track record, and complementary collaboration; reviewers explicitly list 'None' when no weaknesses are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application challenges and shifts current research paradigms through novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application of a new technique (e.g., ribosome profiling) to a field where it has not been used is considered highly innovative ('first for the field', 'clever and cutting edge'). Potential weaknesses include that the method was not developed by the investigators and that it has been used in other systems; reviewers explicitly note whether any significant weaknesses exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses to accomplish the specific aims, including consideration of potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the rationale, clarity of protocols, inclusion of alternative approaches, feasibility, controls, validation plans, and bioinformatics pipelines. Example strengths: 'Well developed rationale', 'Excellent discussion of alternative approaches', 'Inclusion of three major life stages'. Example weaknesses: lack of outlined controls, need for validation of protocol, technical difficulty isolating certain cell forms. Reviewers may recommend additional experiments but also judge fit to the funding mechanism (e.g., scope appropriate for R21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources available to the investigators and whether the scientific environment will contribute to success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider infrastructure, history of productivity at the institution, availability of required facilities (e.g., bioinformatics core), and whether there are few other places with comparable track record and resources. Strengths and weaknesses are explicitly stated; 'Excellent' and 'None' are used when favorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects / Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of whether human subjects are involved and, if so, adequacy of protections and compliance with human subjects regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no human subjects are involved, reviewers state 'Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)' or a human subjects code (e.g., '10-No human subjects involved'). If human subjects are involved, reviewers would evaluate protections, but in this summary the guidance is simply to declare applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals / Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the involvement of vertebrate animals and whether animal care and use are acceptable and compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary records presence of animals (e.g., '30-Vertebrate animals involved - no SRG concerns noted') and a verdict such as 'Acceptable' for vertebrate animal protections. Reviewers indicate acceptability for vertebrate animals and may list concerns if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether proposed work involves biological agents or materials that pose biosafety concerns and whether appropriate protections are described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers mark biohazards as 'Acceptable' or flag issues. In this summary the item is listed as 'Acceptable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for sharing data, model organisms, and other resources generated by the project; reviewers judge completeness and specificity of sharing commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans can be judged Acceptable or Unacceptable. Example critique: 'Unacceptable — The plans to share the data are incomplete in that it is not stated within what timeframe the data will be made publicly available. Please be specific.' Reviewers expect explicit timelines and details for public data release and other sharing mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment and committee recommendation regarding the requested budget and period of support; administrative handling of final award amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may 'Recommend as Requested' or propose adjustments. Administrative note: 'The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations made by reviewers. If an award is planned, the costs will be calculated by Institute grants management staff based on the recommendations outlined below in the COMMITTEE BUDGET RECOMMENDATIONS section.' Committee budget recommendations are recorded separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring procedure and reviewer submission practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules governing how criterion and overall impact scores are produced and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are submitted by individual reviewers prior to the meeting and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score; overall scores (1-9) from voting reviewers are averaged and multiplied by 10 to produce the impact/priority score. This summary references relevant NIH Guide Notices and links to the NIH peer review process for details (e.g., NOT-OD-10-080 and peer_review_process.htm).
